4	the interfaces Waves 4/5/7 consume. Inputs, all read in full or in the cited sections:

21	## 0. Decisions at a glance
22	
23	| # | Decision | Section |
24	|---|----------|---------|
25	| D1 | Definitional Pic = Čech H¹ of the units presheaf on the small Zariski site: **pointed covers** (one open per point), built **on mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1`** fixed-family layer, refinement colimit as a sigma-type quotient, everything in `Type u`. | §2 |
26	| D2 | Group structure **multiplicative**, `CommGroup` carriers, `CommGrpCat.{u}`-valued functors. | §2.4 |
27	| D3 | Relative functor = H_T-coset quotient `Pic((C ⊗ T).left) ⧸ range(snd-pullback)` on `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ`, `CommGrpCat.{u}`-valued. Never the absolute `Pic(C×T)`. | §3 |

One plus suffices because `relPic` is étale-separated (Kleiman 2.5(1) recast; hypothesis discharged by `ex:gc&r`). Consumed as a section variable; discharged by a Wave-4 *def* `jacobianData C`, never `Nonempty` + choice, never a sorried instance. | §5 |

36	## 1. Standing conventions
37	
38	- **Universe discipline: everything at `u`.** `Scheme.{u}`, test category `Over (Spec (.of k))`
39	  with hom-types in `Type u`, all Pic carriers in `Type u`, all functors valued in
40	  `CommGrpCat.{u}`. This is forced by `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`
41	  (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Grp.lean:35`), which couples the universe of the
42	  representing object's homs with the functor's value universe (survey "Universe landmines").
43	  `JacobianData C` itself lives in `Type (u+1)` (it contains a scheme); that is harmless.
44	- **Hypothesis bundle.** Every file uses the frozen variable block
45	  `{k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
46	  [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`, plus the Wave-1 derived instance
47	  `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom` (route Wave-1 item 2) whenever integrality is used.
48	- **Product language.** All products of test objects are the cartesian-monoidal product in
49	  `Over (Spec (.of k))` (`CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Over.lean:34`,
50	  `Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory`, chosen via `Limits.pullback`): `C ⊗ T`, projections
51	  `fst C T`, `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`. This is the vocabulary of the frozen file
52	  (`𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))`, `η[·]`, `Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε`). Descents to `Scheme`-level
53	  pullbacks (`(C ⊗ T).left`) happen only inside cocycle constructions, with the bridge lemmas
54	  confined to `Picard/RelFunctor.lean`. Known wall: `Over.pullback` instance opacity — use the
55	  route rule 9 fixes (point-level `congrArg` calc chains, `erw [Category.comp_id]`).
56	- **Verification bar** (route rule 7): `lake build <Module>` kernel check, then `lean_verify`
57	  axiom audit (`propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` only) on each keystone. LSP advisory only.
58	- Category names verified in the v4.31 checkout: bundled concrete categories are `GrpCat`,
59	  `CommGrpCat`, `CommMonCat` (e.g. `CommMonCat.units : CommMonCat.{u} ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}`,
60	  `Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Adjunctions.lean:202`); bundled group *objects* are
61	  `CategoryTheory.Grp C` (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Grp.lean:82`), the challenge's
62	  `Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))`.

64	---
65	
66	## 2. (A) The definitional Pic carrier
67	
68	**Semantic pin.** For any scheme `X`, the Picard group *of record* is the Čech cohomology
69	`Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site: covers by opens, unit-valued 1-cocycles modulo
70	coboundaries, colimit over refinement. This is recon lesson 1 verbatim, and it is Kleiman's own
71	remark `rk:coh` (§2.11): "for any ringed space `R`, there is a natural isomorphism
72	`Pic(R) = H¹(R, 𝒪_R^*)`" (his eq. 2.11.2 = `eq:2b`, citing Hartshorne III Ex. 4.5).
73	
74	**Semantic-honesty remark (record in the blueprint chapter).** The frozen `Challenge.lean` never
75	mentions `Pic`, line bundles, or invertible sheaves; the only consumers of the carrier are the
76	functors and elements defined in this spec. Therefore the comparison
77	"`CechPic X ≃ {invertible 𝒪_X-modules}/≅`" is **Phase-2 optional** (a `ForMathlib` PR
78	candidate), and no Wave depends on it. What is **Phase-1 mandatory** is that `𝒪(D)`-classes of
79	relative effective divisors be constructible as explicit cocycles from local equations, because
80	`ofCurve` is pinned as `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` (route §3). §2.6 pins that constructor.
81	
82	### 2.1 Index discipline: pointed covers, arbitrary opens
83	
84	```lean
85	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. -/
86	structure Scheme.PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
87	  opens : X → X.Opens
88	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
89	```
90	
91	with the refinement preorder `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`.
92	
93	Decision rationale (each alternative was weighed):
94	
95	- **Not finite covers, not affine covers, not `Set X.Opens`.** Pointed covers give:
96	  (a) *smallness for free* — the index type is the fixed carrier `X : Type u`, so the sigma type
97	  in §2.3 stays in `Type u`; (b) *canonical refinement maps* — a refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰` refines
98	  **indexwise** (`𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`), so the cocycle-restriction map needs no choice of a
99	  reindexing function and no "independence of the refinement map" lemma at the carrier level;
100	  (c) *directedness by pointwise `⊓`* (`(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x := 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x`), so the
101	  refinement colimit is filtered; (d) *clean pullback* — for `f : X ⟶ Y` the pulled-back cover is
102	  `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens (f x))`, again pointed, again indexed by the carrier. Affineness
103	  constraints would break (d) (preimages of affines are not affine); `Set`-indexing breaks (b)
104	  (pullback collapses indices).
105	- Affine or finite covers re-enter as *cofinality lemmas*, not as carrier structure: every
106	  pointed cover is refined by a pointed affine cover (`x ↦` an affine open neighbourhood inside
107	  `𝒰.opens x`; the choice lives inside a `Prop`, so no data escapes). This is where the
108	  2-cover computations of the χ-ledger and the T₀ engine plug in.
109	
110	### 2.2 The cocycle layer: build on `PresheafOfGroups.H1`
111	
112	**Decision: build on mathlib's fixed-family layer**, not hand-rolled. Instantiation:
113	
114	```lean
115	/-- The units presheaf of a scheme, on its small Zariski site. -/
116	def Scheme.unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
117	  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units
118	-- (OPEN-4: if the `forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat` path is absent in v4.31, a ~20-line
119	-- bespoke functor replaces the composition; the statement shape is unchanged.)
120	
121	abbrev Scheme.unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :=
122	  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
123	```
124	
125	Here the site category is the poset `X.Opens`, the family is `𝒰.opens : X → X.Opens`, and
126	mathlib's `OneCochain/OneCocycle/OneCohomologyRelation/IsCohomologous/H1` + `One (H1 G U)`
127	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/NonabelianCohomology/H1.lean:58–197`) come for free. On a poset
128	with infima, the `ev (i j) (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j)`-style cochain is *equivalent* to the
129	classical pair data `g x y ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)` with the cocycle condition on triple infima: homs
130	are subsingletons, so `ev` is determined by its value at `T = 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y` via `ev_precomp`, and
131	`ev_trans` at the triple infimum is the classical condition. **Binding ergonomic requirement**:
132	`Picard/CechH1.lean` must provide the two-way bridge so lane agents never touch `ev` directly:
133	
134	```lean
135	/-- Build a 1-cocycle over a poset with binary infima from classical pair data. -/
136	def PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs
137	    (g : ∀ x y, G.obj (op (𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒰.opens y)))
138	    (hg : ∀ x y z, /- restrictions to the triple infimum satisfy g x y · g y z = g x z -/) :
139	    OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens
140	lemma ev_inf (γ : OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens) (x y) : γ.ev x y ⋯ = ⋯   -- extraction at the infimum
141	```
142	
143	Additions ours to make (all in `Picard/CechH1.lean`, stated generically over any `Cᵒᵖ ⥤
144	CommGrpCat.{w}` — a mathlib-PR candidate, their file's TODO list asks for exactly this):
145	
146	- `Mul/Inv/CommGroup (OneCocycle Gc U)` when the presheaf is commutative-group-valued (the
147	  product of cocycles satisfies `ev_trans` only using commutativity), and the descended
148	  `CommGroup (H1 Gc U)` via `Quot.map₂` (compatibility of `IsCohomologous` with products again
149	  uses commutativity).
150	- Restriction along an indexwise refinement `res : H1 G 𝒰 →* H1 G 𝒱` for `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰`
151	  (on cocycles: restrict values along the inclusions; strictly functorial:
152	  `res_res : res h₂ ∘ res h₁ = res (h₁.trans h₂)` holds on the nose at cochain level).
153	
154	### 2.3 The refinement colimit
155	
156	```lean
157	/-- The definitional Picard group: Čech H¹ of the units presheaf, colimit over pointed covers. -/
158	def Scheme.CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
159	  Quot (fun p q : (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, PresheafOfGroups.H1 ⋯ 𝒰.opens) =>
160	    ∃ 𝒲, ∃ (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1), res h₁ p.2 = res h₂ q.2)
161	```
162	
163	- The relation is an equivalence *because the poset is directed* (common refinement by pointwise
164	  `⊓`) and `res` strictly composes; the standard filtered-colimit argument is elementary and
165	  choice-free.
166	- Universe accounting: `X.PointedCover : Type u`, each `H1 … : Type u` (index `X : Type u`,
167	  values in `Type u`), the sigma is `Type u`, the quotient is `Type u`. **No `ULift` anywhere.**
168	- `CommGroup (X.CechPic)`: multiplication of classes represented on a common refinement;
169	  well-definedness from §2.2's `CommGroup (H1 …)` + `res` being a group hom.
170	- Constructor/eliminator API: `CechPic.mk (𝒰) (γ : OneCocycle …) : X.CechPic`,
171	  `CechPic.ind`, `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff_of_refines`, and the "sanity gate"
172	  `CechPic (Spec (.of K)) ≃* PUnit`-style triviality for fields (one-point space, one cover,
173	  `ev_refl` kills every cocycle) — this is Lane 1's cheap end-to-end test.
174	
175	### 2.4 Group structure: multiplicative, `CommGrpCat`-valued
176	
177	**Decision: multiplicative.** Justification (each item load-bearing):
178	
179	1. The cocycle values are *units of rings*; their native structure is multiplicative, and
180	   `tensor product of line bundles = pointwise multiplication of transition units`,
181	   `dual = pointwise inverse` — recon lesson 1's entire point. An additive carrier would
182	   re-introduce a translation layer at exactly the spot the old draft burned.
183	2. `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` takes `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}` — multiplicative — and
184	   `forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` is the canonical bridge. The old draft's
185	   `AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}` choice cost both a universe bump and an additive/multiplicative
186	   mismatch at the representability gate.
187	3. Mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1` layer (§2.2) is multiplicative.
188	
189	The `ℤ`-valued *degree* (§6) is additive; the interface between the multiplicative Pic and the
190	additive degree is a single `→ ℤ` map with `deg (a * b) = deg a + deg b` — pinned as such, no
191	`Multiplicative ℤ` gymnastics in consumer-facing statements.
192	
193	### 2.5 Functoriality: pullback of cocycles
194	
195	```lean
196	def Scheme.CechPic.map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic
197	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_id (X) : CechPic.map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id _
198	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
199	    CechPic.map (f ≫ g) = (CechPic.map f).comp (CechPic.map g)
200	```
201	
202	On representatives: pull the cover back pointwise through `f.base` (`x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`),
203	pull the units back through `f.app`, restrict. `map_comp` compares the covers
204	`(f ≫ g) ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x))` and `f ⁻¹ᵁ (g ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x)))` — equal opens
205	(`Scheme.preimage_comp`), with the value comparison through `Scheme.Hom.app_comp`; if defeq
206	friction appears, prove it through the refinement relation (both sides restrict to a common
207	refinement) rather than `eqToHom` surgery.
208	
209	### 2.6 Divisor classes as cocycles: the `𝒪(D)` constructor
210	
211	Three constructors, in dependency order. Sign convention (route §3, audited in §8):
212	a local-equation system `(fᵢ)` for an effective `D` produces the class of `𝒪(D)` with
213	transition units `g x y = f x / f y` on overlaps (trivialization of `𝒪(D)` on `𝒰x` by
214	multiplication by `f x`).
215	
216	**(a) Local-equation data → class** (`Picard/DivisorClass.lean`):
217	
218	```lean
219	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor, adapted to a pointed cover. -/
220	structure Scheme.LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
221	  cover : X.PointedCover
222	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
223	  regular : ∀ x, /- eqn x is a nonzerodivisor in every stalk over cover.opens x -/
224	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, IsUnit (/- (eqn x)/(eqn y) as a section on the overlap, i.e.
225	      ∃ u : unit on 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y, (eqn x)|∩ = u * (eqn y)|∩ -/)
226	
227	def Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass (d : X.LocalEquations) : X.CechPic
228	  -- the class of the cocycle (x,y) ↦ the unit u x y with (eqn x)|∩ = u x y • (eqn y)|∩
229	```
230	
231	with: uniqueness of `u x y` (regularity makes the ratio unit unique — this is why `regular` is
232	part of the data), the cocycle identity for `u` (from associativity of the ratios),
233	*independence*: two `LocalEquations` cutting out the same closed subscheme (or related by
234	unitwise rescaling) have equal `picClass`; *multiplicativity*: pointwise product of equations ↦
235	product of classes; *pullback compatibility*: for `f : X' ⟶ X` such that the pulled-back
236	equations are still regular (guaranteed in the relative situation below),
237	`(d.pullback f).picClass = CechPic.map f d.picClass`.
238	
239	**(b) The two geometric instances** (`Picard/GraphDivisor.lean`):
240	
241	- *Point divisor.* For a `k`-point `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C`, the image of `P` is an
242	  effective Cartier divisor on `C.left`: the local ring at the image point is a DVR
243	  (`Curve/StalksDVR.lean`, Wave 1), so a uniformizer spreads to a local equation, and away from
244	  the point the equation `1` works. Output: `pointDivisor P : C.left.LocalEquations` (cover:
245	  a distinguished pointed cover; the choice of uniformizer is data *inside* the construction,
246	  with `picClass`-level independence proven — see the choice-discipline note in §4.4).
247	- *Graph divisor.* The diagonal `Δ ⊂ (C ⊗ C).left` is a relative effective divisor over the
248	  **second** factor: `pr₂|Δ` is an isomorphism onto the base, in particular finite flat of rank
249	  1, and smoothness of `C/k` of relative dimension 1 makes the conormal module invertible, so
250	  the ideal of `Δ` is locally one regular equation. Deliverable:
251	
252	  ```lean
253	  def graphLocalEquations (t : T ⟶ C /- in Over (Spec k) -/) :
254	      ((C ⊗ T).left).LocalEquations   -- local equations for Γ_t := (C ◁ t)-pullback of Δ ⋯
255	  theorem graphLocalEquations_base_change ⋯  -- Γ_{t ∘ g} equations = pullback of Γ_t equations
256	  ```
257	
258	  The base-change stability is *by construction*: `Γ_t` is the pullback of the universal `Δ`
259	  along `C ◁ (t ≫ ⋯)`, and (a)'s pullback compatibility applies because `Δ` is a *relative*
260	  divisor over the test factor (fibers never contain a component of `C`), so regularity
261	  survives every base change. Rank certificate: `𝒪_{Γ_t} ≅ 𝒪_T` as `T`-algebras, so the
262	  finite-flat rank of `Γ_t → T` is 1 — the input for the degree of `abelElement` (§6).
263	  This mathematics is Kleiman `ex:DivC` (§3.8: `X₀ = Div¹_{X/S}` for the smooth locus) and
264	  `rmk:Jac` (§5.26: "Given `t : T → X`, its graph subscheme `Γ_t ⊂ X × T` is a relative
265	  effective divisor"); both read.
266	
267	**(c) The meromorphic bridge** (`Picard/MeromorphicTrivialization.lean`; needed by the degree,
268	see §6.1): for `X` *integral*, every `CechPic` class is a divisor class. Cocycle proof shape:
269	every nonempty open contains the generic point; fix a base index `x₀` and localize the cocycle
270	values `g x x₀` into the function field; these are meromorphic local equations for a Cartier
271	divisor whose class is the given one. (Classical statement: Kleiman quotes it in the proof of
272	`th:qpp&p` (§5.4): "Since `X × T` is integral, there is a divisor `D` such that `𝒪(D) = 𝓛`
273	by [Hartshorne, Ex. II 6.15]".) This file also pins `divisorClass` for *differences*
274	`D₁ − D₂` of effective data as `picClass D₁ * (picClass D₂)⁻¹`.
275	
276	---
277	
278	## 3. (B) The relative functor
279	
280	Recon lesson 3 is binding: the **certified false-axiom trap** (inbox I-0061) is wiring anything
281	to the absolute `Pic(C ×ₖ T)`; the honest functor is the H_T-coset quotient — Kleiman
282	`df:Pfs` (§2.2): "`Pic_{X/S}(T) := Pic(X_T)/Pic(T)`". Kleiman's `df:aPf` discussion (§2.1,
283	read) is the semantic audit anchor for *why* the absolute functor "is never representable".
284	
285	```lean
286	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
287	
288	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T`
289	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
290	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
291	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ (Scheme.CechPic.map (CartesianMonoidalCategory.snd C T).left).range
292	-- CommGroup instance: QuotientGroup on the CommGroup of §2.3.
293	
294	/-- The relative Picard functor. -/
295	def relPicFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
296	```
297	
298	- **Exact quotient relation**: `[L] = [L']` in `relPic T` iff
299	  `L * L'⁻¹ ∈ (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range` — i.e. iff `L ≅ L' ⊗ pr_T^* N` for some class
300	  `N` on `T`, which in the cocycle model is literally a range condition; no `Nonempty (≅)`
301	  propositions anywhere.
302	- **Evaluation and restriction.** For `g : T' ⟶ T` in `Over (Spec (.of k))`, the map
303	  `relPicFunctor.map g.op` is descent of `CechPic.map ((C ◁ g).left)` to the quotients;
304	  well-defined by the monoidal naturality `(C ◁ g) ≫ snd C T = snd C T' ≫ g`. Functor laws
305	  from `CechPic.map_id/map_comp` plus `QuotientGroup.map` functoriality.
306	- **Universe target**: `CommGrpCat.{u}`, per §1. The functor category
307	  `(Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}` is legitimate (`Over (Spec k) : Type (u+1)` with
308	  `Type u` homs, `CommGrpCat.{u} : Type (u+1)` with `Type u` homs).
309	- Also provided here (consumed by §4 and Wave 7): naturality in the curve,
310	  `relPicMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) : relPicFunctor C ⟶ relPicFunctor C'` (pullback along
311	  `g ▷ T`), strictly functorial in `g`; and the statement of the **base-field shuffle**: for
312	  `L/k` and `T' : Over (Spec (.of L))`, a canonical iso
313	  `relPic (C_L) T' ≃* relPic C ((Over.map (Spec.map _)).obj T')` induced by the scheme
314	  isomorphism `(C_L ⊗_L T').left ≅ (C ⊗_k T'ₖ).left` (`pullbackAssoc`-type; the survey's
315	  `AlgebraicGeometry/Pullbacks.lean` toolkit), compatible with the H-quotients on both sides.
316

355	### 4.2 The three options, weighed
356	
357	**(i) Hand-rolled plus-construction.** Define
358	`PicEt(T) := colim_{étale covers T'→T} ker(relPic T' ⇉ relPic (T' ×_T T'))` (equalizer form —
359	the plus needs no triple-overlap condition). One plus yields a sheaf iff the input presheaf is
360	separated; `relPic` **is** étale- (even fppf-) separated by Kleiman 2.5(1), whose hypothesis
361	holds by `ex:gc&r`. Cost: the separatedness proof (a genuine descent argument, §4.4), cover
362	smallness/indexing, colimit plumbing. Benefit: construction-canonical, evaluates concretely,
363	`relPic → PicEt` is a unit map usable everywhere, and over test schemes where a section exists
364	the unit is bijective *as a theorem* (2.5(2) recast) — exactly what Wave 4 needs over `k'`.
365	
366	**(ii) Define `PicEt` only via 2.5-comparison where sections exist + descent data elsewhere.**
367	Rejected. A piecewise definition is either non-canonical (it depends on which case a test
368	scheme falls into, and for `baseChangeIso` the case-split differs between `C/k` and `C_L/L`)
369	or secretly equal to (i) with the plus spelled out by hand. Every interface (group law, degree,
370	functoriality in `C`, base-field shuffle) would need case-coherence lemmas. The *content* of
371	(ii) — the comparison bijections — survives as the pair of theorems (C1), (C2) in §4.4.
372	
373	**(iii) Representability over `k'` + Galois descent, with `PicEt := the functor J represents`.**
374	Rejected **as a definition**, retained **as the Wave-4 proof strategy**. The blocker is
375	exactly the one the route anticipates: `baseChangeIso` must compare `(J_C)_L` with `J_{C_L}`,
376	and both must be recognized as representing *the same construction-canonical functor* over `L`.
377	If `PicEt_k` is defined as `Hom(−, J)`, the `RepresentableBy` datum is a tautology carrying no
378	information, and the comparison of `(J_C)_L` with `J_{C_L}` has no common third functor to
379	factor through — one would have to smuggle the construction back in, per-instance, at every
380	coherence. **Resolution (binding):** the functor is defined by construction (option (i)); the
381	`k'`-plus-descent argument is how Wave 4 *produces* the `RepresentableBy` datum; after Wave 4,
382	nothing downstream ever unfolds `J`, only the datum.

384	### 4.3 The decision, in two layers
385	
386	**Layer 1 — affine tests, presented covers** (`Picard/EtaleCovers.lean`, `Picard/PicEtAff.lean`).
387	
388	For `T` with `T.left` affine (`A := Γ(T.left, ⊤)`), an étale cover index is a *presentation*:
389	
390	```lean
391	/-- A presented affine étale cover of `Spec A`: a chosen finite presentation of an étale,
392	faithfully flat `A`-algebra. -/
393	structure EtCover (A : CommRingCat.{u}) : Type u where
394	  n m : ℕ
395	  relations : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A
396	  -- carrier B := (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ⧸ (span of relations)
397	  etale : Algebra.Etale A B
398	  surjective : /- Spec B → Spec A surjective (with étale + fp this gives faithful flatness) -/
399	```
400	
401	- `Type u`-small by construction, choice-free, and closed under the operations the plus needs:
402	  a *refinement* of covers is a `T`-morphism `Spec B' → Spec B`; *directedness* via
403	  `B ⊗[A] B'` (which has an explicit presentation); *base change* along `A → A'` re-presents
404	  with the same polynomials.
405	- Descent classes and the one-step plus, equalizer form:
406	
407	```lean
408	def descentClasses (E : EtCover A) : Subgroup (relPic C (T' E)) :=
409	  -- ker of (pullback along pr₁) / (pullback along pr₂) into relPic C (T' E ⊗_T T' E)
410	def PicEtAff (T /- affine -/) : Type u :=
411	  -- Σ (E : EtCover A), descentClasses E, quotiented by refinement, CommGroup
412	def picEtAffUnit : relPic C T →* PicEtAff C T   -- classes with the tautological descent datum
413	```
414	
415	- *Refinement-map independence* (the lemma that makes the colimit canonical): two `T`-morphisms
416	  `h₁ h₂ : Spec B'' → Spec B'` induce the same map on `descentClasses`, because
417	  `(h₁, h₂) : Spec B'' → Spec B' ×_T Spec B'` pulls the descent-datum equation
418	  `p₁^*λ = p₂^*λ` back to `h₁^*λ = h₂^*λ`. One line, but it is the keystone of
419	  well-definedness; pin it as a named lemma.
420	- Zariski refinements are included automatically: a standard affine cover
421	  `Spec (∏ᵢ A_{fᵢ}) → Spec A` is a presented étale cover, so the plus also performs the
422	  Zariski sheafification on affines — needed for `relPic`-vs-`PicEt` comparisons to be honest.
423	- Over a *field* base `Spec K`, single-factor refinement works (any factor field of an étale
424	  `K`-algebra already covers the point), so **field-extension covers are cofinal** — pin this
425	  lemma; it makes `PicEtAff C (Spec K) = colim_{K'/K fin. sep.} (Galois-stable part of
426	  relPic over K')`, the form the degree (§6) and Wave 4 consume.
427	
428	**Layer 2 — all test objects** (`Picard/PicEt.lean`).
429	
430	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` forces the functor to be defined on **all** of `Over (Spec (.of k))`
431	(the frozen `instGrpObj` leaves no choice), while the plus is only well-behaved on affines. The
432	extension is the canonical right-Kan-style limit over affine opens:
433	
434	```lean
435	def picEt (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
436	  -- lim over the poset of affine opens U ≤ T.left of PicEtAff C (T restricted to U),
437	  -- i.e. compatible families (λ_U)_U; CommGroup pointwise
438	def picEtFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
439	def picEtUnit : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C
440	theorem picEt_affine_iso (hT : IsAffine T.left) : picEt C T ≃* PicEtAff C T ⋯
441	```
442	
443	For affine `T`, `T.left` is the top of its own affine-opens poset, so the limit collapses to
444	`PicEtAff C T` (canonical iso, not defeq — one lemma). Functoriality in `T` maps a family
445	`(λ_V)_V` over `T` to the family `(res λ_V)` indexed by pairs `U ⊆ f⁻¹V` — the comma-limit
446	construction. `picEt` is a Zariski sheaf by construction; the étale sheaf sequence is claimed
447	(and needed) **only for affine `T` with presented covers** — this is recorded as the honest
448	semantic pin in the blueprint: "`picEtFunctor` restricted to affine tests *is* the étale
449	sheafification of `relPicFunctor` there (one plus of a separated presheaf), and is its canonical
450	Zariski-continuous extension elsewhere." **OPEN-1**: whether Layer 2 is implemented as this
451	bespoke limit or through mathlib's dense-subsite machinery
452	(`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Affine.lean`: `isCoverDense_toOver_Spec` + `IsCoverDense` sheaf
453	extension); closing criterion in §9.
454	
455	Also in `Picard/PicEt.lean`, stated at this level because Wave 7 consumes them:
456	
457	- `picEtMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) : picEtFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C'` with `mapCurve_id/comp`
458	  (descend `relPicMapCurve` through the plus and the limit; pullback preserves descent data).
459	- The **base-field shuffle**, étale level: for `L/k` and `T' : Over (Spec (.of L))`,
460	  `picEtBaseField : picEt (C_L) T' ≃* picEt C (T'ₖ)` — descends from §3's `relPic` shuffle
461	  because an étale cover of `T'` is *the same thing* over `L` and over `k` (étaleness and
462	  presentations are `T'`-intrinsic; this is precisely why the plus is indexed by covers **of
463	  the test scheme**, never of the base). Natural in `T'`, compatible with units and with
464	  `picEtMapCurve`.

466	### 4.4 Why one plus suffices: the separatedness ledger
467	
468	**(C1) Separatedness** (`Picard/Separatedness.lean`): for affine `T` and a presented étale
469	cover `E`, the map `relPic C T → relPic C (T' E)` is injective. This is Kleiman 2.5(1)
470	restricted to what we consume, recast on cocycles. Proof ledger (all pieces named because they
471	are shared bricks):
472	
473	1. `sectionsBaseChange` (`Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean`): for `V ⊆ C.left` affine open
474	   and a `k`-algebra `A`, `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, V_A) ≅ Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A`, naturally.
475	   *Shared with*: the T₀ dual-numbers engine (`A = k[ε]`, recon lesson 7) and the χ-ledger over
476	   field extensions (`A = K`). One brick, three consumers.
477	2. `universalSections` (`Picard/UniversalSections.lean`): `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, ⊤) = A` for
478	   every `k`-algebra `A` — the two-cover H⁰ slice: the complex
479	   `Γ(V₀) ⊕ Γ(V₁) → Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` has `H⁰ = k` (Wave 1), stays exact under the flat `⊗[k] A`
480	   by 1. This is our discharge of Kleiman's `ex:gc&r` hypothesis in the form actually consumed.
481	3. `prPullback_injective`: `CechPic.map (snd C T).left` is injective for affine `T` — a unit
482	   cocycle on `C ⊗ T` trivializing must have come from `T`, because
483	   `𝒪ˣ((C ⊗ V).left) = Γ(V)ˣ` by 2 (applied on an affine pointed cover of `T`). Hence the
484	   H_T-quotient loses nothing it shouldn't, and "which `N`" in a `pr^*N`-equation is unique.
485	4. `Descent/InvertibleModule.lean` (pure algebra, PR-candidate): along a faithfully flat ring
486	   map `A → B`, an invertible `B`-module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
487	   `A`-module, uniquely up to canonical isomorphism. (Survey: this exists **nowhere** in
488	   mathlib — "no effective descent of modules"; it is the honest algebraic core of both (C1)
489	   and (C2).)
490	5. Assembly (Kleiman's 2.5(1) argument recast): a class `λ ∈ relPic C T` dying on the cover
491	   gives, via 3 applied over `T'` and `T' ×_T T'`, a line-bundle class `n'` on `T'` with a
492	   descent datum along `Spec B → Spec A`; by 4 it descends to `n` on `T`, and `λ = pr^* n`
493	   follows from 3 again. Hence `λ = 0` in the quotient.

665	general-coefficients carrier `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` (TwoCover.lean:91): feed it the
666	**equalizer-presented twisted sheaf** `F_g(W) := {(s₀, s₁) | s₀ = g·s₁ on W ⊓ V₀ ⊓ V₁}` for a
667	2-cover cocycle `g`; the required `Subsingleton (HModule' F Vᵢ 1)` instances transport along
668	`F_g|Vᵢ ≅ 𝒪|Vᵢ` — which holds *by construction* of `F_g`, so **no new affine-vanishing
669	engine is needed**. (Coordination note to Wave 2; verified against the TwoCover hypotheses,
670	which demand nothing but the two vanishing instances and `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`.)
671	
672	### 6.2 `Pic⁰` as the degree-kernel subfunctor
673	
674	`Picard/DegreeZero.lean`:
675	
676	```lean
677	/-- Degree of an étale Picard class at a field-valued point of the test scheme. -/
678	def degAt (λ : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
679	    (t : Over.mk (Spec.map ⋯) ⟶ T /- a `Spec K`-point of `T` over `k` -/) : ℤ
680	  -- restrict λ along t into picEt C (Spec K); field-extension covers are cofinal there
681	  -- (§4.3), so λ|_{Spec K} is represented over some finite separable K′/K; take deg over K′
682	  -- ((E-ii) applied over K′); well-defined by (E-iv).
683	
684	/-- The degree-0 subfunctor — the functor the Jacobian represents. -/
685	def pic0Functor (C) ⋯ : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
686	  -- T ↦ {λ : picEt C T | ∀ K t, degAt λ t = 0}, a subgroup; restriction maps restrict
687	  -- because a field point of T′ composes to a field point of T (this is WHY the definition
688	  -- quantifies over all field-valued points rather than points of the space: subfunctor
689	  -- stability is definitional).
690	```
691	
692	Audit: this matches Kleiman's fiberwise-strata pattern (his `P^φ` in the proof of 4.8 is cut
693	out by a fiberwise-χ condition `eq:phi` "for all `t ∈ T`", well-defined "because cohomology
694	commutes with flat base change" — our (E-iv)). Degree-*constancy* in families (local constancy
695	of `t ↦ degAt`) is **not needed for the definition** and is deliberately deferred: it needs the
696	rigid two-term pushforward engine (Mumford AV II.5) and belongs to Wave 4/5.
697	
698	**The Abel element** (`Picard/AbelElement.lean`), test scheme `T := C`:
699	
700	```lean
701	def abelElement (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : pic0 C C :=
702	  -- picEtUnit of [𝒪(Δ)] * [𝒪(fst⁻¹ P)]⁻¹ on (C ⊗ C).left  (graph of 𝟙 minus constant-P),
703	  -- degree-0 certificate: at a field point t, deg 𝒪(Γ_t) = 1 (graph has finite-flat rank 1,
704	  -- §2.6(b), via (E-i)) and deg 𝒪(P_K) = 1 (P is a k-point; (E-i) again). 1 − 1 = 0.
705	theorem abelElement_map_point : (pic0Functor C).map P.op (abelElement P) = 1
706	theorem abelElement_baseField ⋯   -- shuffle ∘ base-change of abelElement = abelElement of ε ≫ P_L
707	```

709	Then `ofCurve P := d.rep.homEquiv.symm (abelElement P)` realizes route §3's
710	`t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]`: for any `t : T ⟶ C`, naturality gives
711	`t ≫ ofCurve P = homEquiv.symm ([𝒪(Γ_t)] * [𝒪(P_T)]⁻¹)` — the pin, verbatim.
712	
713	Degree-0 preservation under `picEtMapCurve g` (needed so `pic0MapCurve` exists for Wave 7's
714	`functor`): at a field point, `g` base-changes to a morphism of curves over `K`; it is constant
715	(pullback class trivial since `Pic(Spec κ) = 1`) or finite (then `deg (g^*L) = (deg g)·(deg L)`
716	via `finrank` multiplicativity on divisor classes); either way degree 0 is preserved. The
717	dichotomy brick is flagged in §4.6.

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Grp.Basic

/-! # The cohomology of a sheaf of groups in degree 1

In this file, we shall define the cohomology in degree 1 of a sheaf
of groups (TODO).

Currently, given a presheaf of groups `G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat` and a family
of objects `U : I → C`, we define 1-cochains/1-cocycles/H^1 with values
in `G` over `U`. (This definition neither requires the assumption that `G`
is a sheaf, nor that `U` covers the terminal object.)
As we do not assume that `G` is a presheaf of abelian groups, this
cohomology theory is only defined in low degrees; in the abelian
case, it would be a particular case of Čech cohomology (TODO).

## TODO

* show that if `1 ⟶ G₁ ⟶ G₂ ⟶ G₃ ⟶ 1` is a short exact sequence of sheaves
  of groups, and `x₃` is a global section of `G₃` which can be locally lifted
  to a section of `G₂`, there is an associated canonical cohomology class of `G₁`
  which is trivial iff `x₃` can be lifted to a global section of `G₂`.
  (This should hold more generally if `G₂` is a sheaf of sets on which `G₁` acts
  freely, and `G₃` is the quotient sheaf.)
* deduce a similar result for abelian sheaves
* when the notion of quasi-coherent sheaves on schemes is defined, show that
  if `0 ⟶ Q ⟶ M ⟶ N ⟶ 0` is an exact sequence of abelian sheaves over a scheme `X`
  and `Q` is the underlying sheaf of a quasi-coherent sheaf, then `M(U) ⟶ N(U)`
  is surjective for any affine open `U`.
* take the colimit of `OneCohomology G U` over all covering families `U` (for
  a Grothendieck topology)

# References

* [J. Frenkel, *Cohomologie non abélienne et espaces fibrés*][frenkel1957]

-/

@[expose] public section

universe w' w v u

namespace CategoryTheory

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

namespace PresheafOfGroups

variable (G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}) {I : Type w'} (U : I → C)

/-- A zero cochain consists of a family of sections. -/
def ZeroCochain := ∀ (i : I), G.obj (Opposite.op (U i))

instance : Group (ZeroCochain G U) := Pi.group

namespace Cochain₀

@[simp]
lemma one_apply (i : I) : (1 : ZeroCochain G U) i = 1 := rfl

@[simp]
lemma inv_apply (γ : ZeroCochain G U) (i : I) : γ⁻¹ i = (γ i)⁻¹ := rfl

@[simp]
lemma mul_apply (γ₁ γ₂ : ZeroCochain G U) (i : I) : (γ₁ * γ₂) i = γ₁ i * γ₂ i := rfl

end Cochain₀

/-- A 1-cochain of a presheaf of groups `G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat` on a family `U : I → C` of objects
consists of the data of an element in `G.obj (Opposite.op T)` whenever we have elements
`i` and `j` in `I` and maps `a : T ⟶ U i` and `b : T ⟶ U j`, and it must satisfy a compatibility
with respect to precomposition. (When the binary product of `U i` and `U j` exists, this
data for all `T`, `a` and `b` corresponds to the data of a section of `G` on this product.) -/
@[ext]
structure OneCochain where
  /-- the data involved in a 1-cochain -/
  ev (i j : I) ⦃T : C⦄ (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) : G.obj (Opposite.op T)
  ev_precomp (i j : I) ⦃T T' : C⦄ (φ : T ⟶ T') (a : T' ⟶ U i) (b : T' ⟶ U j) :
    G.map φ.op (ev i j a b) = ev i j (φ ≫ a) (φ ≫ b) := by aesop

namespace OneCochain

attribute [simp] OneCochain.ev_precomp

instance : One (OneCochain G U) where
  one := { ev := fun _ _ _ _ _ ↦ 1 }

@[simp]
lemma one_ev (i j : I) {T : C} (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) :
    (1 : OneCochain G U).ev i j a b = 1 := rfl

variable {G U}

instance : Mul (OneCochain G U) where
  mul γ₁ γ₂ := { ev := fun i j _ a b ↦ γ₁.ev i j a b * γ₂.ev i j a b }

@[simp]
lemma mul_ev (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) {T : C} (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) :
    (γ₁ * γ₂).ev i j a b = γ₁.ev i j a b * γ₂.ev i j a b := rfl

instance : Inv (OneCochain G U) where
  inv γ := { ev := fun i j _ a b ↦ (γ.ev i j a b)⁻¹ }

@[simp]
lemma inv_ev (γ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) {T : C} (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) :
    (γ⁻¹).ev i j a b = (γ.ev i j a b)⁻¹ := rfl

instance : Group (OneCochain G U) where
  mul_assoc _ _ _ := by ext; apply mul_assoc
  one_mul _ := by ext; apply one_mul
  mul_one _ := by ext; apply mul_one
  inv_mul_cancel _ := by ext; apply inv_mul_cancel

end OneCochain

end OneCochain

/-- A 1-cocycle is a 1-cochain which satisfies the cocycle condition. -/
structure OneCocycle extends OneCochain G U where
  ev_trans (i j k : I) ⦃T : C⦄ (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) (c : T ⟶ U k) :
      ev i j a b * ev j k b c = ev i k a c := by aesop

namespace OneCocycle

instance : One (OneCocycle G U) where
  one := OneCocycle.mk 1

@[simp]
lemma one_toOneCochain : (1 : OneCocycle G U).toOneCochain = 1 := rfl

@[simp]
lemma ev_refl (γ : OneCocycle G U) (i : I) ⦃T : C⦄ (a : T ⟶ U i) :
    γ.ev i i a a = 1 := by
  simpa using γ.ev_trans i i i a a a

lemma ev_symm (γ : OneCocycle G U) (i j : I) ⦃T : C⦄ (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) :
    γ.ev i j a b = (γ.ev j i b a)⁻¹ := by
  rw [← mul_left_inj (γ.ev j i b a), γ.ev_trans i j i a b a,
    ev_refl, inv_mul_cancel]

end OneCocycle

variable {G U}

/-- The assertion that two cochains in `OneCochain G U` are cohomologous via
an explicit zero-cochain. -/
def OneCohomologyRelation (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCochain G U) (α : ZeroCochain G U) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i j : I) ⦃T : C⦄ (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j),
    G.map a.op (α i) * γ₁.ev i j a b = γ₂.ev i j a b * G.map b.op (α j)

namespace OneCohomologyRelation

lemma refl (γ : OneCochain G U) : OneCohomologyRelation γ γ 1 := fun _ _ _ _ _ ↦ by simp

lemma symm {γ₁ γ₂ : OneCochain G U} {α : ZeroCochain G U} (h : OneCohomologyRelation γ₁ γ₂ α) :
    OneCohomologyRelation γ₂ γ₁ α⁻¹ := fun i j T a b ↦ by
  rw [← mul_left_inj (G.map b.op (α j)), mul_assoc, ← h i j a b,
    mul_assoc, Cochain₀.inv_apply, map_inv, inv_mul_cancel_left,
    Cochain₀.inv_apply, map_inv, inv_mul_cancel, mul_one]

lemma trans {γ₁ γ₂ γ₃ : OneCochain G U} {α β : ZeroCochain G U}
    (h₁₂ : OneCohomologyRelation γ₁ γ₂ α) (h₂₃ : OneCohomologyRelation γ₂ γ₃ β) :
    OneCohomologyRelation γ₁ γ₃ (β * α) := fun i j T a b ↦ by
  dsimp
  rw [map_mul, map_mul, mul_assoc, h₁₂ i j a b, ← mul_assoc,
    h₂₃ i j a b, mul_assoc]

end OneCohomologyRelation

namespace OneCocycle

/-- The cohomology (equivalence) relation on 1-cocycles. -/
def IsCohomologous (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle G U) : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : ZeroCochain G U), OneCohomologyRelation γ₁.toOneCochain γ₂.toOneCochain α

variable (G U)

lemma equivalence_isCohomologous :
    _root_.Equivalence (IsCohomologous (G := G) (U := U)) where
  refl γ := ⟨_, OneCohomologyRelation.refl γ.toOneCochain⟩
  symm := by
    rintro γ₁ γ₂ ⟨α, h⟩
    exact ⟨_, h.symm⟩
  trans := by
    rintro γ₁ γ₂ γ₂ ⟨α, h⟩ ⟨β, h'⟩
    exact ⟨_, h.trans h'⟩

end OneCocycle

variable (G U) in
/-- The cohomology in degree 1 of a presheaf of groups
`G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat` on a family of objects `U : I → C`. -/
def H1 := Quot (OneCocycle.IsCohomologous (G := G) (U := U))

/-- The cohomology class of a 1-cocycle. -/
def OneCocycle.class (γ : OneCocycle G U) : H1 G U := Quot.mk _ γ

instance : One (H1 G U) where
  one := OneCocycle.class 1

lemma OneCocycle.class_eq_iff (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle G U) :
    γ₁.class = γ₂.class ↔ γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂ :=
  (equivalence_isCohomologous _ _).quot_mk_eq_iff _ _

lemma OneCocycle.IsCohomologous.class_eq {γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle G U} (h : γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂) :
    γ₁.class = γ₂.class :=
  Quot.sound h

end PresheafOfGroups

end CategoryTheory

1	# Route decision — the mathematical architecture of the rebuild
2	
3	*2026-07-11, Fable-5 design session. Inputs: a 5-agent survey (mathlib v4.31.0 capability
4	inventory; old-draft map; Kleiman/FGA route DAG; alternative-routes survey; operational
5	lessons). Survey reports are archived in the session scratchpad; their load-bearing
6	conclusions are restated here so this document is self-contained.*
7	
8	This document fixes the route for all 14 protected targets in
9	`AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` and the design rules every wave must follow.
10	It is the map; the blueprint is the mathematics; the Lean tree is the proof.
11	
12	## 1. The route in one paragraph
13	
14	**`Jacobian C := Pic⁰_{C/k}`**, the identity component of the scheme representing the
15	étale-sheafified relative Picard functor of `C/k` (Kleiman, *The Picard Scheme*, FGA
16	Explained ch. 5). Representability is the central mountain (Grothendieck's Thm 4.8,
17	specialized hard to a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a field).
18	The Albanese universal property is proved Milne-style (*Abelian Varieties* III.6.1):
19	symmetric powers `C^(g) → J` birational, rational maps into abelian varieties extend
20	(Milne I.3.2 = I.3.1 + Lemma 3.3), rigidity makes the factorization a homomorphism,
21	uniqueness descends from `k̄` to `k`. The genus is `g(C) := dim_k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` with
22	`H¹` the derived-functor cohomology of the Zariski site of `C` valued in `ModuleCat k`,
23	computed by a pinned 2-affine-cover Mayer–Vietoris cokernel and proved finite by the
24	two-lattice ladder over a finite map `C → ℙ¹`. Every functorial target (`functor`,
25	`baseChangeIso`, the coherences) is a uniqueness-of-representing-object corollary of a
26	single pinned `RepresentableBy` datum — never a `Classical.choice` extraction.
27	
28	Why not the alternatives (survey verdicts):
29	
30	- **Weil group-chunk construction (Sym^g + birational group law): rejected.** Its
31	  obligations (scheme quotients by finite groups, relative divisors,
32	  cohomology-and-base-change, Weil's globalization theorem, plus a descent problem for
33	  pointless curves — the challenge's `Jacobian` takes **no rational point**) meet or
34	  exceed the FGA debt, and the functorial targets would still have to be re-derived
35	  through the Pic functor afterwards (Milne III.7.6). FGA's Thm 4.8 needs no point;
36	  that is a structural advantage for this exact statement file.
37	- **Kleiman's own Albanese derivation (`rmk:Alb`): rejected** — it outsources dual
38	  abelian varieties, autoduality (`Ĵ ≅ J`, [EGK Thm 2.1], unproved in our references)
39	  and projectivity of abelian varieties. Milne III.6.1 is strictly lighter and its
40	  ingredients (Sym^g, Riemann–Roch) are shared with the `Div^d`-representability leg,
41	  so their cost is amortized.

132	   inequality; principal divisors have degree 0. Feeds N2 (projectivity), Div^d, and

136	### Wave 3 — the Picard functor and the gated spine

140	   post-mortem endorses the cocycle model).

142	   schemes; group-valued; degree map; `Pic⁰` sub-functor.

144	    pinned `RepresentableBy` + the instance package. Downstream waves consume
145	    `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable. NEVER a sorried instance

160	13. Tangent space `T₀Pic = H¹(C,𝒪)` (dual numbers, truncated exponential) [S];
161	    smoothness via geometric reducedness at 0 + `smooth_of_grpObj` [S];
162	    `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C)` assembly [S].

166	    first for Albanese).
167	15. Geometric irreducibility: identity-component theory (`lem:agps(3)`: `G⁰` open-closed,
168	    finite type, geometrically irreducible, formation commutes with field extension) [S].
169	    This single lemma also powers `baseChangeIso`.
170	
171	### Wave 6 — Albanese [RG mountain #2]
172	16. Sym^r C as a scheme (finite-group quotient via Γ-stable affine covers — the old
173	    draft's Galois-quotient engine design, re-derived) [S–RG]; smoothness of `C^(g)` [S];
174	    `Div^r ≅ C^(r)` [S] (shared with Wave 4!).
175	17. Rational-map extension chain: Milne I.3.1 [S], Lemma 3.3 (the four audited substeps;
176	    two were proved in the old draft) [RG], Thm 3.2 [R given both].
177	18. Milne III.6.1 assembly over `k̄` [S]; uniqueness-first Galois descent to `k` [S];
178	    `ofCurve`, `comp_ofCurve`, `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` discharge.
179	
180	### Wave 7 — the functorial layer (cheap **by design** if Wave 3's pin is respected)
181	19. `functor` (pullback of line bundles = precomposition on represented functors;
182	    laws by uniqueness) [S-tedious]; 20. `baseChangeIso` (étale-site base-change formal
183	    identity + `(Pic⁰)_L = (Pic_L)⁰` from #15) [S]; 21. coherences + `baseChange_ofCurve`
184	    (uniqueness of isos intertwining pinned universal elements) [R–S given the pin].
185	
186	## 5. Design rules (binding for every wave; distilled from the campaign post-mortems)
187	
188	1. **Keystone funnel.** Every wave funnels to one keystone with a wide parallel base;
189	   state the *narrowest* form a consumer needs (degree-1-only vanishing beat the full
190	   Čech-to-derived comparison; i=0 affine base-change bricks beat the `R^i f_*` engine).
191	2. **Statement audit before proof.** Every pinned statement gets a semantic audit against
192	   the source before anyone proves it (the old campaign shipped three false-as-pinned
193	   statements; each cost runs). Counterexamples for rejected pins go in the blueprint.
194	3. **No sorried data, no choice-extracted witnesses.** Deep pillars are gated as Prop
195	   classes or explicit structure hypotheses; `sorry` never inhabits a def/instance.
196	4. **One pinned universal element.** `Jacobian`, `functor`, `baseChangeIso` are all
197	   defined through the same `RepresentableBy` datum; coherences become uniqueness.
198	5. **No monoidal sheaf categories; no global adele space; no general `R^i f_*` engine;
199	   no Quot schemes.** Each is a measured multi-week detour whose consumers have
200	   cheaper curve-specific substitutes.
201	6. **Files ≤ 500 lines; mathlib naming; blueprint chapter per Lean directory,
202	   1-to-1 nodes, `\leanok` only after kernel check; `\source{}` only after reading.**
203	7. **Verification bar**: `lake build <Module>` (kernel), then `lean_verify` axiom audit
204	   (`propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` only). LSP is advisory; `lake env lean`
205	   is a false oracle (lakefile sets `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`).
206	8. **Uniform genus.** No genus-0 fork anywhere; `J = Pic⁰` uniformly (the old draft
207	   deleted a weeks-long genus-0 lane).
208	9. **Known Lean walls + fixes** (from the ops mining, use as first resort):
209	   `Over.pullback` instance-opacity → point-level `congrArg` calc chains; defeq-blocked
210	   `𝟙` → `erw [Category.comp_id]`; functor laws by `subst`-shaped proofs; scoped
211	   `maxHeartbeats` bumps ≤ 1M (never stack past it — restructure); repeated `binop%`
212	   products hoisted into a named def; `GrpObj` is data → `letI`; `open scoped MonObj`.
213	
214	## 6. What "done" means, phase by phase
215	
216	- **Phase 1**: all 14 protected declarations sorry-free; `lake build` green;
217	  `#print axioms` on each = standard three; blueprint every node `\leanok` with sources.
218	- **Phase 2** (only after green): REVIEW.md anchors for the three headline theorems,
219	  code↔paper correspondence tightening, `ForMathlib/` extraction of the general bricks
220	  (smooth⇒geometrically reduced, identity-component theory, rigidity, MV `ModuleCat k`
221	  slice, finite-group quotients, Speiser descent are the obvious PR candidates).

8	# Global sections of a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field
9	
10	The keystone of the curve substrate: for a scheme `X` proper and geometrically integral over a
11	field `K`, the structure map induces an isomorphism `K ≅ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
12	
13	* `AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`:
14	  the honest general form — `f.appTop : Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` is bijective.
15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral` and the bundle instance
16	  `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hom_appTop_of_geometricallyReduced`: the instance-friendly forms.
17	
18	## Proof sketch
19	
20	Write `A := Γ(X, ⊤)`. By Mathlib's properness facts (`isField_of_universallyClosed`,
21	`finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`), `A` is a field, finite over `K`. Base change `f` along
22	`Spec A ⟶ Spec K`: the total space `X_A` is again proper and geometrically integral over the
23	field `A`, so `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` is a field as well. Flat base change of sections
24	(`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`) exhibits `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` as the pushout
25	`A ⊗[K] A`. A pushout of a field extension along itself being a field forces `K ⟶ A` to be an
26	*epimorphism* of rings (`CommRingCat.epi_of_isPushout_of_isField`: the codiagonal
27	`A ⊗[K] A ⟶ A` is injective, being a ring map out of a field, and surjective, being split by
28	`inl`; hence `inl` is an isomorphism and the two coprojections agree). A finite ring
29	epimorphism is surjective (`RingHom.surjective_of_epi_of_finite`), and any ring map out of a
30	field is injective.
31	
32	Geometric reducedness enters only through `GeometricallyIntegral`; for the curve bundle of the
33	challenge it is supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Limits
41	
42	namespace CommRingCat
43	
44	/-- If a pushout square of commutative rings has isomorphic legs (`e : C ≅ B` intertwining
45	`ψ` and `φ`) and its pushout `D` is a field, then `φ` is an epimorphism.
46	
47	This is the classical "diagonal" criterion: the codiagonal `μ : D ⟶ B` determined by
48	`𝟙 B` and `e.hom` is injective (a ring map out of a field into a nontrivial ring) and split
49	surjective, hence an isomorphism; so `inl = e.inv ≫ inr`, which makes `φ` epi. -/
50	lemma epi_of_isPushout_of_isField {A B C D : CommRingCat.{u}}
51	    {φ : A ⟶ B} {ψ : A ⟶ C} {inl : B ⟶ D} {inr : C ⟶ D}
52	    (H : IsPushout φ ψ inl inr) (hD : IsField D) [Nontrivial B]
53	    (e : C ≅ B) (he : ψ ≫ e.hom = φ) : Epi φ := by
54	  letI : Field D := hD.toField
55	  -- the codiagonal
56	  let μ : D ⟶ B := H.desc (𝟙 B) e.hom (by rw [Category.comp_id, he])
57	  have hμinl : inl ≫ μ = 𝟙 B := H.inl_desc _ _ _
58	  have hμinr : inr ≫ μ = e.hom := H.inr_desc _ _ _
59	  have : IsIso μ := by
60	    refine (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective μ).mpr ⟨μ.hom.injective, fun b ↦ ⟨inl b, ?_⟩⟩
61	    simpa using congr($(hμinl) b)
62	  -- the two coprojections agree up to `e`
63	  have key : e.inv ≫ inr = inl := by
64	    rw [← cancel_mono μ, Category.assoc, hμinr, hμinl, Iso.inv_hom_id]
65	  refine ⟨fun {W} u v huv ↦ ?_⟩
66	  have w : φ ≫ u = ψ ≫ (e.hom ≫ v) := by
67	    rw [← Category.assoc, he]; exact huv
68	  calc u = inl ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := (H.inl_desc _ _ _).symm
69	    _ = e.inv ≫ inr ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := by rw [← Category.assoc, key]
70	    _ = e.inv ≫ e.hom ≫ v := by rw [H.inr_desc]
71	    _ = v := by rw [Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
72	
73	end CommRingCat
74	
75	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
76	
77	/-- Bundled variant of `AlgebraicGeometry.isField_of_universallyClosed`: if `X` is an integral
78	scheme, universally closed over the spectrum of a (bundled) commutative ring `R` that is a
79	field, then `Γ(X, ⊤)` is a field. -/

open Order in
lemma height_of_isClosed {X : Scheme} {x : X} (hx : IsClosed {x}) : height x = 0 := by
  simp only [height_eq_zero]
  intro b _
  obtain rfl | h := eq_or_ne b x
  · assumption
  · have := IsClosed.not_specializes hx rfl h
    contradiction

namespace Hom

variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) {U U' : Y.Opens} {V V' : X.Opens}

/-- Given a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`, and open `U ⊆ Y`,
this is the induced map `Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U)`.

This is treated as a suffix in lemma names. -/
abbrev app (U : Y.Opens) : Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U) :=
  f.c.app (op U)

/-- Given a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`, this is the induced map `Γ(Y, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)`.
This is treated as a suffix in lemma names. -/
abbrev appTop : Γ(Y, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤) :=
  f.app ⊤

@[reassoc]
lemma naturality (i : op U' ⟶ op U) :
    Y.presheaf.map i ≫ f.app U = f.app U' ≫ X.presheaf.map ((Opens.map f.base).map i.unop).op :=
  f.c.naturality i

/-- Given a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`, and open sets `U ⊆ Y`, `V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U`,
this is the induced map `Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V)`.

This is treated as a suffix in lemma names. -/
def appLE (U : Y.Opens) (V : X.Opens) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) : Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V) :=
  f.app U ≫ X.presheaf.map (homOfLE e).op

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma appLE_map (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (i : op V ⟶ op V') :
    f.appLE U V e ≫ X.presheaf.map i = f.appLE U V' (i.unop.le.trans e) := by
  rw [Hom.appLE, Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp]
  rfl

@[reassoc]
lemma appLE_map' (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (i : V = V') :
    f.appLE U V' (i ▸ e) ≫ X.presheaf.map (eqToHom i).op = f.appLE U V e :=
  appLE_map _ _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma map_appLE (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (i : op U' ⟶ op U) :
    Y.presheaf.map i ≫ f.appLE U V e =
      f.appLE U' V (e.trans ((Opens.map f.base).map i.unop).le) := by
  rw [Hom.appLE, f.naturality_assoc, ← Functor.map_comp]
  rfl

@[reassoc]
lemma map_appLE' (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (i : U' = U) :
    Y.presheaf.map (eqToHom i).op ≫ f.appLE U' V (i ▸ e) = f.appLE U V e :=
  map_appLE _ _ _

lemma app_eq_appLE {U : Y.Opens} :
    f.app U = f.appLE U _ le_rfl := by
  simp [Hom.appLE]

lemma appLE_eq_app {U : Y.Opens} :
    f.appLE U (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl = f.app U :=
  (app_eq_appLE f).symm

lemma appLE_congr (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (e₁ : U = U') (e₂ : V = V')

    P (f.appLE U V e) ↔ P (f.appLE U' V' (e₁ ▸ e₂ ▸ e)) := by
  subst e₁; subst e₂; rfl

/-- A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` induces a local ring homomorphism from
`Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)` to `X.presheaf.stalk x` for any `x : X`. -/
def stalkMap (x : X) : Y.presheaf.stalk (f x) ⟶ X.presheaf.stalk x :=
  f.toLRSHom.stalkMap x

protected lemma ext {f g : X ⟶ Y} (h_base : f.base = g.base)

theorem id_app {X : Scheme} (U : X.Opens) :

@[simp]
theorem id_appTop {X : Scheme} :

@[reassoc]
theorem comp_toLRSHom {X Y Z : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :

@[simp, reassoc]
theorem comp_base {X Y Z : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    (f ≫ g).base = f.base ≫ g.base :=

theorem comp_apply {X Y Z : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (x : X) :
    (f ≫ g) x = g (f x) := by
  simp

@[simp, reassoc] -- reassoc lemma does not need `simp`
theorem comp_app {X Y Z : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (U) :
    (f ≫ g).app U = g.app U ≫ f.app _ :=
  rfl

@[simp, reassoc] -- reassoc lemma does not need `simp`
theorem comp_appTop {X Y Z : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :

@[reassoc]
theorem appLE_comp_appLE {X Y Z : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (U V W e₁ e₂) :
    g.appLE U V e₁ ≫ f.appLE V W e₂ =

    (f ≫ g).appLE U V e = g.app U ≫ f.appLE _ V e := by
  rw [g.app_eq_appLE, appLE_comp_appLE]

theorem congr_app {X Y : Scheme} {f g : X ⟶ Y} (e : f = g) (U) :
    f.app U = g.app U ≫ X.presheaf.map (eqToHom (by subst e; rfl)).op := by
  subst e; simp

theorem app_eq {X Y : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) {U V : Y.Opens} (e : U = V) :
    f.app U =

theorem eqToHom_app {X Y : Scheme} (e : X = Y) (U) :

/-!
# The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge

For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` covered by two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, this file
computes the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `k`-modules on
the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) as an explicit cokernel of a map of section
modules:

`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪ₖ) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀⊓U₁} - s₁|_{U₀⊓U₁})`

(`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`, with the cokernel carrier
`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`). This is the computational access point for the genus
of a curve: `genus C = finrank k H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C)` becomes the corank of an explicit map of
function spaces.

**Hypotheses actually used**: `X` any scheme over `Spec k`, `IsAffineOpen U₀`,
`IsAffineOpen U₁`, `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`. In particular *no* affineness (or even
quasi-compactness) hypothesis on the intersection `U₀ ⊓ U₁` is needed — unlike for the
classical Čech-complex identification, the derived-functor Mayer–Vietoris sequence of
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris` is exact regardless, and affineness of the
two pieces alone kills their `H¹'` (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`).

## Main declarations

* `Scheme.twoCoverSquare` — the Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the
  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.
* `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — the general-coefficients form: for any sheaf `F` of
  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,
  `HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k] F(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range(moduleDiff)` (reusable for twisted sheaves).
* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.
* `TwoCover.H1Cok k X U₀ U₁` — the cokernel carrier `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`.
* `TwoCover.delta` — the connecting map `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
  ("class of a section on the overlap").
====

import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Grp.Adjunctions

/-!
# The units presheaf of a scheme

For a scheme `X`, this file defines the presheaf `𝒪_X^*` of unit groups of the structure
sheaf on the small Zariski site (the poset `X.Opens`), valued in `CommGrpCat`, together
with the element-level interface used by the Čech `H¹` layer of the Picard group:

* restriction of a unit section along `V ≤ U` is `Units.map` of the ring-level restriction;
* pullback of a unit section along a morphism of schemes, packaged as
  `Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE` (the unit-group analogue of `Scheme.Hom.appLE`), with the same
  composition/restriction calculus as `appLE`.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsPresheaf`: the units presheaf
  `X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units`, a functor
  `(X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsPresheaf_map_apply`: restriction of unit sections,
  element form.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE`: for `f : X ⟶ Y`, `V : Y.Opens`,
  `U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, the group homomorphism `Γ(Y, V)ˣ →* Γ(X, U)ˣ`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map`, `Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE`,
  `Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE`, `Scheme.id_unitsAppLE`: the calculus mirroring
  `appLE_map`, `map_appLE`, `appLE_comp_appLE` and `id_app` at the unit level.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}

/-- The units presheaf `𝒪_X^*` of a scheme `X`, on its small Zariski site: the composite
of the structure presheaf with the units functor, valued in commutative groups. -/
def unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units

lemma unitsPresheaf_obj (U : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ) :
    X.unitsPresheaf.obj U = CommGrpCat.of Γ(X, unop U)ˣ :=
  rfl

lemma unitsPresheaf_map {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) :
    X.unitsPresheaf.map i = CommGrpCat.ofHom (Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom) :=
  rfl

/-- Element form of the restriction maps of the units presheaf. This is the interface
through which cocycle computations reach the `Units` API. -/
@[simp]
lemma unitsPresheaf_map_apply {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) (u : Γ(X, unop U)ˣ) :
    X.unitsPresheaf.map i u = Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom u :=
  rfl

/-- The composite with the forgetful functor to `GrpCat` (the shape consumed by
`CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle`), element form. -/
@[simp]
lemma unitsPresheaf_forget₂_map_apply {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) (u : Γ(X, unop U)ˣ) :
    (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).map i u
      = Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom u :=
  rfl

namespace Hom

variable (f : X ⟶ Y) {V V' : Y.Opens} {U U' : X.Opens}

/-- The action of a morphism of schemes on unit sections: for `V : Y.Opens` and
`U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, the induced group homomorphism `Γ(Y, V)ˣ →* Γ(X, U)ˣ`. This is the
unit-group analogue of `Scheme.Hom.appLE` and is treated as a suffix in lemma names. -/
def unitsAppLE (f : X.Hom Y) (V : Y.Opens) (U : X.Opens) (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) :
    Γ(Y, V)ˣ →* Γ(X, U)ˣ :=
  Units.map (f.appLE V U e).hom

@[simp]
lemma coe_unitsAppLE (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (u : Γ(Y, V)ˣ) :
    (f.unitsAppLE V U e u : Γ(X, U)) = f.appLE V U e u :=
  rfl

/-- Restriction after pullback: the unit-level mirror of `Scheme.Hom.appLE_map`. -/
@[simp]
lemma unitsAppLE_map (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (i : op U ⟶ op U') (u : Γ(Y, V)ˣ) :
    Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom (f.unitsAppLE V U e u)
      = f.unitsAppLE V U' (i.unop.le.trans e) u := by
  ext
  simp only [Units.coe_map, coe_unitsAppLE]
  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, appLE_map]

/-- Pullback after restriction: the unit-level mirror of `Scheme.Hom.map_appLE`. -/
@[simp]
lemma map_unitsAppLE (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (i : op V' ⟶ op V) (u : Γ(Y, V')ˣ) :
    f.unitsAppLE V U e (Units.map (Y.presheaf.map i).hom u)
      = f.unitsAppLE V' U (e.trans ((Opens.map f.base).map i.unop).le) u := by
  ext
  simp only [Units.coe_map, coe_unitsAppLE]
  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, map_appLE]

end Hom

/-- Pullback along a composite: the unit-level mirror of `Scheme.appLE_comp_appLE`. -/
@[simp]
lemma unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) {W : Z.Opens} {V : Y.Opens}
    {U : X.Opens} (e₁ : V ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ W) (e₂ : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (u : Γ(Z, W)ˣ) :
    f.unitsAppLE V U e₂ (g.unitsAppLE W V e₁ u)
      = (f ≫ g).unitsAppLE W U (e₂.trans ((Opens.map f.base).map (homOfLE e₁)).le) u := by
  ext
  simp only [Units.coe_map, Hom.coe_unitsAppLE]
  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, appLE_comp_appLE]

/-- Pullback along the identity is restriction: the unit-level mirror of `Scheme.id_app`. -/
lemma id_unitsAppLE {U V : X.Opens} (e : U ≤ (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X) ⁻¹ᵁ V) (u : Γ(X, V)ˣ) :
    (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).unitsAppLE V U e u
      = Units.map (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE e).op).hom u := by
  ext
  simp only [Units.coe_map, Hom.coe_unitsAppLE]
  rw [Hom.appLE, Scheme.id_app, Category.id_comp]

end Scheme

end AlgebraicGeometry

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.NonabelianCohomology.H1
import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Grp.Basic
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Preorder
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsPresheaf

/-!
# Čech 1-cocycles: restriction, poset pair data, and commutative group structure

This file extends Mathlib's fixed-family nonabelian Čech layer
(`CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle`, `H1`) with the three pieces of
infrastructure needed for a Čech-style Picard group (all stated generically; this file
is a Mathlib-PR candidate and contains no algebraic geometry):

1. **Restriction along an indexwise refinement.** For families `U V : I → C` and maps
   `f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i`, cochains/cocycles/`H1`-classes restrict along `f`, strictly
   functorially (`res_res` holds on the nose at the cochain level).
2. **The poset bridge.** Over a poset with binary infima, a 1-cochain is determined by
   its values `evInf i j` at the infima `U i ⊓ U j` (`ev_eq_evInf`), and a 1-cocycle can
   be built from classical pair data satisfying the cocycle condition at triple infima
   (`OneCocycle.ofPairs`). Consumers never need to touch `ev` directly.
3. **Commutative group structure.** When the presheaf takes values in `CommGrpCat`,
   1-cocycles form a commutative group under pointwise multiplication (the cocycle
   condition for products needs commutativity) and this descends to `H1`; restriction
   is then a group homomorphism (`H1.resHom`).

## Main declarations

* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCochain.res`, `OneCocycle.res`, `H1.res`:
  restriction along an indexwise refinement, with `res_res` and `res_id`.
* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCochain.evInf`, `ev_eq_evInf`: over a poset with
  binary infima, evaluation of a cochain at `U i ⊓ U j` determines it.
* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs`: the classical construction of a
  cocycle from pair data `g i j` on binary infima with the triple-infimum condition.
* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf`: the coboundary
  relation in classical pair form.
* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.H1.subsingleton_of_forall_le`: if the members of the
  family are mutually comparable (e.g. all equal to a top element), `H1` is trivial.
* `CommGroup (OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U)` and
  `CommGroup (H1 (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U)` for `G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.H1.resHom`: restriction as a group homomorphism.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe w' w v u

open CategoryTheory Opposite

namespace CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {I : Type w'}

/-! ## Restriction along an indexwise refinement -/

section Res

variable {G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}} {U V W : I → C}

namespace OneCochain

/-- Restriction of a 1-cochain along an indexwise refinement `f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i`. -/
def res (γ : OneCochain G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : OneCochain G V where
  ev i j _ a b := γ.ev i j (a ≫ f i) (b ≫ f j)
  ev_precomp i j T T' φ a b := by simp

@[simp]
lemma res_ev (γ : OneCochain G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (i j : I) {T : C}
    (a : T ⟶ V i) (b : T ⟶ V j) :
    (γ.res f).ev i j a b = γ.ev i j (a ≫ f i) (b ≫ f j) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma one_res (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : (1 : OneCochain G U).res f = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma mul_res (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCochain G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) :
    (γ₁ * γ₂).res f = γ₁.res f * γ₂.res f :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma inv_res (γ : OneCochain G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) :
    (γ⁻¹).res f = (γ.res f)⁻¹ :=
  rfl

/-- Restriction is strictly functorial at the cochain level. -/
@[simp]
lemma res_res (γ : OneCochain G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (g : ∀ i, W i ⟶ V i) :
    (γ.res f).res g = γ.res (fun i ↦ g i ≫ f i) := by
  ext i j T a b
  simp

@[simp]
lemma res_id (γ : OneCochain G U) : γ.res (fun i ↦ 𝟙 (U i)) = γ := by
  ext i j T a b
  simp

end OneCochain

namespace OneCocycle

lemma toOneCochain_injective :
    Function.Injective (toOneCochain : OneCocycle G U → OneCochain G U) := by
  rintro ⟨γ₁, h₁⟩ ⟨γ₂, h₂⟩ h
  simpa using h

@[ext]
lemma ext {γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle G U} (h : γ₁.toOneCochain = γ₂.toOneCochain) : γ₁ = γ₂ :=
  toOneCochain_injective h

/-- Restriction of a 1-cocycle along an indexwise refinement `f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i`. -/
def res (γ : OneCocycle G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : OneCocycle G V where
  toOneCochain := γ.toOneCochain.res f
  ev_trans i j k T a b c := by
    simp only [OneCochain.res_ev]
    exact γ.ev_trans i j k (a ≫ f i) (b ≫ f j) (c ≫ f k)

@[simp]
lemma res_toOneCochain (γ : OneCocycle G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) :
    (γ.res f).toOneCochain = γ.toOneCochain.res f :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma res_ev (γ : OneCocycle G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (i j : I) {T : C}
    (a : T ⟶ V i) (b : T ⟶ V j) :
    (γ.res f).ev i j a b = γ.ev i j (a ≫ f i) (b ≫ f j) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma one_res (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : (1 : OneCocycle G U).res f = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma res_res (γ : OneCocycle G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (g : ∀ i, W i ⟶ V i) :
    (γ.res f).res g = γ.res (fun i ↦ g i ≫ f i) :=
  ext (γ.toOneCochain.res_res f g)

@[simp]
lemma res_id (γ : OneCocycle G U) : γ.res (fun i ↦ 𝟙 (U i)) = γ :=
  ext γ.toOneCochain.res_id

end OneCocycle

lemma OneCohomologyRelation.res {γ₁ γ₂ : OneCochain G U} {α : ZeroCochain G U}
    (h : OneCohomologyRelation γ₁ γ₂ α) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) :
    OneCohomologyRelation (γ₁.res f) (γ₂.res f) (fun i ↦ G.map (f i).op (α i)) := by
  intro i j T a b
  simpa [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp]
    using h i j (a ≫ f i) (b ≫ f j)

lemma OneCocycle.IsCohomologous.res {γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle G U} (h : γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂)
    (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : (γ₁.res f).IsCohomologous (γ₂.res f) := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := h
  exact ⟨_, hα.res f⟩

/-- Restriction of degree-one cohomology classes along an indexwise refinement. -/
def H1.res (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : H1 G U → H1 G V :=
  Quot.map (·.res f) (fun _ _ h ↦ h.res f)

@[simp]
lemma H1.res_class (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (γ : OneCocycle G U) :
    H1.res f γ.class = (γ.res f).class :=
  rfl

/-- Restriction of `H1` classes is strictly functorial. -/
lemma H1.res_res (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (g : ∀ i, W i ⟶ V i) (x : H1 G U) :
    H1.res g (H1.res f x) = H1.res (fun i ↦ g i ≫ f i) x := by
  induction x using Quot.ind with
  | _ γ => exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (γ.res_res f g)

@[simp]
lemma H1.res_id (x : H1 G U) : H1.res (fun i ↦ 𝟙 (U i)) x = x := by
  induction x using Quot.ind with
  | _ γ => exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) γ.res_id

@[simp]
lemma H1.res_one (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : H1.res f (1 : H1 G U) = 1 :=
  rfl

end Res

/-! ## The poset bridge: pair data on binary infima -/

section Poset

variable {P : Type u} [SemilatticeInf P] {G : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}} {U : I → P}

private lemma map_map (G : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}) {a b c : P} (h₁ : a ≤ b) (h₂ : b ≤ c)
    (x : G.obj (op c)) :
    G.map (homOfLE h₁).op (G.map (homOfLE h₂).op x) = G.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op x := by
  rw [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]

namespace OneCochain

/-- The value of a 1-cochain on the binary infimum `U i ⊓ U j`. Over a poset with binary
infima this determines the whole cochain, see `ev_eq_evInf`. -/
def evInf (γ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) : G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j)) :=
  γ.ev i j (homOfLE inf_le_left) (homOfLE inf_le_right)

/-- Over a poset, a 1-cochain is determined by its values on binary infima. -/
lemma ev_eq_evInf (γ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) {T : P} (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) :
    γ.ev i j a b = G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le)).op (γ.evInf i j) := by
  rw [evInf, γ.ev_precomp]
  congr 1 <;> exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

end OneCochain

namespace OneCocycle

/-- The value of a 1-cocycle on the binary infimum `U i ⊓ U j`. -/
abbrev evInf (γ : OneCocycle G U) (i j : I) : G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j)) :=
  γ.toOneCochain.evInf i j

/-- The classical cocycle condition for the pair values of a 1-cocycle: on the triple
infimum, `g i j * g j k = g i k`. -/
lemma evInf_trans (γ : OneCocycle G U) (i j k : I) :
    G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U j)).op (γ.evInf i j) *
        G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U j ⊓ U k)).op
          (γ.evInf j k) =
      G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U k)).op
        (γ.evInf i k) := by
  have h := γ.ev_trans i j k (T := U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k)
    (homOfLE (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left)) (homOfLE (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right))
    (homOfLE inf_le_right)
  simp only [γ.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf] at h
  exact h

/-- Build a 1-cocycle over a poset with binary infima from classical pair data: values
`g i j` on the binary infima satisfying the cocycle condition on triple infima. -/
def ofPairs (g : ∀ i j, G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j)))
    (hg : ∀ i j k,
      G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U j)).op (g i j) *
          G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U j ⊓ U k)).op
            (g j k) =
        G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U k)).op
          (g i k)) :
    OneCocycle G U where
  ev i j _ a b := G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le)).op (g i j)
  ev_precomp i j T T' φ a b := map_map G φ.le (le_inf a.le b.le) (g i j)
  ev_trans i j k T a b c := by
    rw [← map_map G (le_inf (le_inf a.le b.le) c.le) inf_le_left (g i j),
      ← map_map G (le_inf (le_inf a.le b.le) c.le) (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right) (g j k),
      ← map_map G (le_inf (le_inf a.le b.le) c.le) (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left) (g i k),
      ← map_mul, hg i j k]

@[simp]
lemma ofPairs_ev (g : ∀ i j, G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j))) (hg) (i j : I) {T : P}
    (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) :
    (ofPairs g hg).ev i j a b = G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le)).op (g i j) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma evInf_ofPairs (g : ∀ i j, G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j))) (hg) (i j : I) :
    (ofPairs g hg).evInf i j = g i j := by
  show G.map (homOfLE _).op (g i j) = g i j
  rw [show homOfLE _ = 𝟙 (U i ⊓ U j) from Subsingleton.elim _ _, op_id, G.map_id]
  rfl

/-- Round trip: rebuilding a 1-cocycle from its pair values gives it back. -/
lemma ofPairs_evInf (γ : OneCocycle G U) :
    ofPairs (fun i j ↦ γ.evInf i j) (fun i j k ↦ γ.evInf_trans i j k) = γ := by
  ext1
  ext i j T a b
  exact (γ.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf i j a b).symm

/-- The coboundary relation in classical pair form: two 1-cocycles over a poset with
binary infima are cohomologous iff there are sections `α i` on the `U i` conjugating the
pair values into each other. -/
lemma isCohomologous_iff_evInf (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle G U) :
    γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂ ↔ ∃ α : ZeroCochain G U, ∀ i j,
      G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i)).op (α i) * γ₁.evInf i j =
        γ₂.evInf i j * G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U j)).op (α j) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨α, hα⟩
    exact ⟨α, fun i j ↦ hα i j (homOfLE inf_le_left) (homOfLE inf_le_right)⟩
  · rintro ⟨α, hα⟩
    refine ⟨α, fun i j T a b ↦ ?_⟩
    have h' := congrArg (G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le : T ≤ U i ⊓ U j)).op ·) (hα i j)
    simp only [map_mul, map_map] at h'
    rw [γ₁.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf i j a b, γ₂.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf i j a b]
    exact h'

end OneCocycle

/-- If the members of the family are mutually comparable (e.g. the family is constant,
as for a cover of a one-point space), then `H1` is trivial: every 1-cocycle is a
coboundary via `α i := γ.evInf`-type data at a base index. -/
theorem H1.subsingleton_of_forall_le (G : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}) (U : I → P)
    (h : ∀ i j, U i ≤ U j) : Subsingleton (H1 G U) := by
  have key : ∀ γ : OneCocycle G U, (1 : OneCocycle G U).IsCohomologous γ := by
    intro γ
    cases isEmpty_or_nonempty I with
    | inl hI => exact ⟨1, fun i ↦ isEmptyElim i⟩
    | inr hI =>
      obtain ⟨i₀⟩ := hI
      refine ⟨fun i ↦ γ.ev i i₀ (𝟙 (U i)) (homOfLE (h i i₀)), fun i j T a b ↦ ?_⟩
      rw [OneCocycle.one_toOneCochain, OneCochain.one_ev, mul_one, OneCochain.ev_precomp,
        Category.comp_id, ← γ.ev_trans i j i₀ a b (b ≫ homOfLE (h j i₀)),
        Subsingleton.elim (a ≫ homOfLE (h i i₀)) (b ≫ homOfLE (h j i₀))]
  refine ⟨fun x y ↦ ?_⟩
  induction x using Quot.ind with
  | _ γ =>
    induction y using Quot.ind with
    | _ δ =>
      exact Quot.sound
        (((OneCocycle.equivalence_isCohomologous G U).symm (key γ)).trans (key δ))
